questions.q: Why can a fresh start help you change?
a: It creates distance from past failures and a new perspective
It guarantees you will not relapse
It gives you more free time than usual
It makes other people expect more of you
questions.why: Lesson one says a fresh start separates old unmet goals from new ones, giving you a different outlook.

a: Pairing a hard task with something you enjoy
Removing all temptations from your home
Rewarding yourself only after a month
Doing two difficult tasks at once
questions.why: Lesson two describes linking a pleasant activity, like a favorite show, to a challenging one such as exercise.

a: Adding scores, badges or rewards to everyday tasks
Turning your goals into a competitive sport
Playing games instead of working
Letting an app set all your deadlines
questions.why: Lesson two says game elements like points and badges make real-world tasks more fun and motivating.

a: A system that restricts your choices to prevent temptation
A contract that pays you for finishing early
A friend who checks on your progress
A calendar that blocks out free time
questions.why: Lesson two defines it as a self-imposed limit, such as blocking distracting apps during work hours.

questions.q: What did the Air Force Academy study show about peers?
a: Cadets with stronger peers earned higher grades
Cadets who studied alone outperformed others
Peer groups had no effect on academic results
Cadets with more friends dropped out more often
questions.why: Lesson three says a hundred-point rise in a squadron's average verbal SAT score came with a 0.4 higher GPA.
